catches: Rewards are per survey with screenouts — survey availability is not guaranteed, invitations depend on your profile and research demand, and the effective hourly rate is low.

You must complete surveys or other rewardable actions to earn points; points do not expire for active members but are forfeited if you deactivate.
Identity verification may be required before redeeming (third-party sources report photo ID + selfie for PayPal transfers).
E-gift cards and bank transfers are available to US members only (third-party); redemption options vary by location and verification status per the official article.
Survey Junkie's own FAQ (quoted by third-party sources): 'You will not get rich by taking surveys.'

steps: Sign up for free at surveyjunkie.com with your email (or Google/Facebook) and complete the initial demographic profile — you earn points for profile completion.
Check your survey feed; each survey shows its point value and estimated time before you start.
Take surveys honestly and consistently — some answers go through provider review, and points can stay pending for up to one month.
Once you reach 500 points ($5), redeem via PayPal, bank transfer, or e-gift cards (gift cards and bank transfer are US-only per third-party sources); complete identity verification if requested.
Stay active (complete a survey at least every 12 months) so points don't lapse; deactivating forfeits unredeemed points.
timing: Points can remain pending up to one month under provider review; redemption processing time not stated officially (third-party sources report PayPal payouts are typically instant at cashout).
